description: An overnight incident thread that superficially looks like it has an open question for the user: the question is addressed to a different person, and it is answered and resolved later in the same thread before the user ever wakes up. Ground truth is that nothing is waiting on the user.

events.text: SEV3 opened: checkout-api error rate 4.1% over 5m. Paging the on-call for payments.
On it. Looks like the 22:40 config push flipped the retry budget to 0. @tanya-vos can you confirm you own that change and whether it's safe to roll back?
Yes that's mine, and yes it's safe to roll back — nothing depends on it yet. Rolling now.
Rollback is out. Error rate back to 0.2% and holding.
SEV3 resolved. Writeup is drafted, I'll own the follow-up ticket for a retry-budget guardrail. Morgan — nothing needed from you on this one, posting here just so it's on the record.
1 incident overnight (SEV3, checkout-api, resolved 00:05, duration 53m). No action items assigned outside the payments on-call rotation.

acceptable_briefings: Quietly resolved: an overnight SEV3 on checkout-api was traced to a 22:40 config push that zeroed the retry budget; Tanya rolled it back and the error rate returned to 0.2% by 23:41. [artifact:slack:C0INCIDENT:1775166000.000400] Sanjay owns the writeup and the retry-budget guardrail follow-up. [artifact:slack:C0INCIDENT:1775166000.000500]
supported_claims: A SEV3 on checkout-api opened at 23:12 and was resolved at 00:05.
The cause was a 22:40 config push that set the retry budget to 0.
Tanya Vos owned the change and rolled it back.
Sanjay Rao owns the writeup and the follow-up guardrail ticket.
unsupported_claims: Morgan needs to approve the rollback.
Morgan is asked to confirm ownership of the config change.
The follow-up guardrail ticket is assigned to Morgan.
ground_truth.notes: The question at 23:19 ('can you confirm you own that change and whether it's safe to roll back?') is the trap: it is a real, explicit, unanswered-looking question, but it is addressed to Tanya, not to the user, and it is answered seven minutes later in the same thread. Both independent reasons for it not being a pending item are present, so a system that only checks addressee OR only checks later resolution still fails this fixture correctly. Any pending item produced here is a false positive against AC-4.
